cards.text: Ishmael, a man from the royal family, has struck down Gedaliah, the governor the king of Babylon appointed, and now everybody's scared of the Chaldeans (Jer 41:1-2, 18). So the army commanders, Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah and all the people, from the least to the greatest, come to Jeremiah the prophet. They ask him to pray for this remnant, because out of many, only a few are left, like the last three cookies in a box that just went around the whole office.

cards.question: The commanders and the people want Jeremiah to pray for them. What do they want the LORD to tell them?

answers.text: The way to walk and what to do
How long Babylon will rule them
Who their next governor will be

cards.question: Jeremiah agrees to pray for the remnant, but says he'll only pass along the good news.

cards.text: Then the people make Jeremiah a promise and ask the LORD Himself to be a true and faithful witness against them if they don't keep it. Friend, that's not a pinky swear, that's signing your name in PERMANENT MARKER.

cards.question: The people promise Jeremiah they'll obey the LORD's answer only if it's pleasant.

cards.text: After ten days, the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah. TEN DAYS of everybody staring at those three little dots in the group chat!

Jeremiah calls together Johanan, the commanders and all the people, from the least to the greatest, to hear the answer from the LORD, the God of Israel. Everybody packs in like the whole office when the boss says, "Quick announcement in the break room."

cards.question: The LORD's answer starts with an if. If the remnant does what, He'll build them up and not tear them down?

cards.text: Build up, not tear down, plant, not uproot, and God even says He'll relent of the disaster He has brought on them. Friend, if somebody had offered me that back in the junk drawer, I'd have jumped out so fast the dust wouldn't have known I left.

cards.question: The LORD tells the remnant not to be ___ of the king of Babylon.
Why does the LORD say the remnant doesn't need to fear the king of Babylon?

answers.text: He is with them to save them
The king has gone back home
The king has made peace with them

cards.text: And it keeps getting BETTER. God says He'll show them compassion, and the king of Babylon, the very one they're so scared of, will show them compassion too.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll show the remnant compassion, and the king of Babylon will too. What does the LORD say comes with that compassion?

answers.text: Being restored to their own land
Being given a king of their own

cards.text: That's the good if. And you KNOW a second if is coming, because there's always a second if: what if the remnant says, 'We will not stay in this land,' and disobeys the voice of the LORD?

cards.question: The LORD's second if pictures the remnant saying they'll go live in the land of ___ instead.
In the LORD's second if, what does the remnant say they won't face once they're living in Egypt?

cards.text: No war, no ram's horn, no hunger for bread. Egypt sounds like a travel ad with a palm tree on it, but now comes the word of the LORD for the remnant of Judah, if they're determined to go there and live.

cards.question: The remnant fears the sword and dreads the famine. If they go to Egypt, what does the LORD say the sword and famine will do?
The LORD says a few of those who go to live in Egypt will escape the disaster.

cards.text: Then God points back to Jerusalem. Just as His anger and wrath were poured out on the people living there, He says His wrath will be poured out on the remnant if they go to Egypt.

cards.question: If the remnant goes to Egypt, what does the LORD say they will never see again?

cards.text: Jeremiah makes it plain: "The LORD has told you, O remnant of Judah, 'Do not go to Egypt.' Know for sure that I have warned you today!" Friend, that's not a hint, that's a smoke alarm going off at three in the morning.

cards.question: Jeremiah looks back at how the people sent him to pray and promised to do whatever the LORD said. He tells them they have ___ themselves.
Jeremiah tells the remnant they have obeyed the voice of the LORD in everything He sent him to tell them.

cards.text: They asked for the LORD's answer, promised to do every word, and then didn't obey it. That's ME asking my phone for directions and then driving the other way while it begs me to make a U-turn.

cards.question: Where does Jeremiah say the remnant will die by sword and famine and plague?

answers.text: In the place they want to live
On the road back to Mizpah

cards.text: Jeremiah closes with 'know for sure,' his second one in this warning, and when a prophet says it twice, that's no suggestion. We'll stop right here, friend, but this story's got more road ahead.
